axiam_sdk

Official Python client SDK for AXIAM (Access eXtended Identity and Authorization Management).

Re-exports the public surface: the sync AxiamClient and async AsyncAxiamClient REST entry points, the AuthError/AuthzError/ NetworkError exception taxonomy (CONTRACT.md §2), and the request/response models (LoginResult, User, AccessCheck, AccessResult, BatchCheckResult, UserInfo). See CONTRACT.md §1-§10 for the cross-language behavioral contract this SDK conforms to.

This module MUST remain importable with ONLY the runtime dependencies declared in [project.dependencies] (httpx, grpcio, aio-pika, pydantic, PyJWT) — the optional web-framework integrations (axiam_sdk.fastapi, axiam_sdk.django, see [project.optional-dependencies]) MUST NOT be imported from here.

class DecisionMemo: 
 78class DecisionMemo:
 79    """A bounded, TTL-clamped decision memo.
 80
 81    ``ttl_ms == 0`` means **disabled** — not "cache for zero milliseconds".
 82    That is the default, and both :meth:`get` and :meth:`set` become no-ops.
 83
 84    Thread-safe: the sync client is commonly shared across a thread pool, and a
 85    cache that corrupted under concurrency would be a worse bug than the one it
 86    is optimising away.
 87    """
 88
 89    __slots__ = ("_ttl_ms", "_entries", "_now", "_lock")
 90
 91    def __init__(self, ttl_ms: float = 0.0, now: Callable[[], float] | None = None) -> None:
 92        """
 93        :param ttl_ms: requested TTL in milliseconds; ``0`` disables the memo and
 94            any value above :data:`MAX_TTL_MS` is clamped to it.
 95        :param now: injected monotonic clock in seconds, so the TTL can be
 96            tested without waiting.
 97        """
 98        self._ttl_ms = min(max(float(ttl_ms), 0.0), MAX_TTL_MS)
 99        self._entries: OrderedDict[str, tuple[object, float]] = OrderedDict()
100        self._now = now if now is not None else time.monotonic
101        self._lock = threading.Lock()
102
103    @property
104    def enabled(self) -> bool:
105        """Whether this memo does anything. ``False`` for the default config."""
106        return self._ttl_ms > 0
107
108    @property
109    def effective_ttl_ms(self) -> float:
110        """The TTL after clamping."""
111        return self._ttl_ms
112
113    def get(self, key: str) -> object | None:
114        """A live decision for *key*, if one is memoized and unexpired."""
115        if not self.enabled:
116            return None
117        with self._lock:
118            entry = self._entries.get(key)
119            if entry is None:
120                return None
121            decision, stored_at = entry
122            if (self._now() - stored_at) * 1000.0 >= self._ttl_ms:
123                del self._entries[key]
124                return None
125            # Returned whole, including ``reason_code``: §17.1 rule 5 forbids
126            # returning ``allowed`` while dropping the code, which would make
127            # the field intermittently absent — worse than never having had it.
128            return decision
129
130    def set(self, key: str, decision: object) -> None:
131        """Memoize a decision the server actually returned.
132
133        Callers must only reach here on success. §17.1 rule 7 forbids
134        negative-caching a failure: memoizing a transport error as a deny would
135        turn a blip into a TTL-long outage, and memoizing it as an allow is
136        unthinkable.
137        """
138        if not self.enabled:
139            return
140        with self._lock:
141            self._entries.pop(key, None)
142            self._entries[key] = (decision, self._now())
143            while len(self._entries) > _MAX_ENTRIES:
144                self._entries.popitem(last=False)
145
146    def clear(self) -> None:
147        """Drop every entry (§17.1 rule 9).
148
149        Called on login, verify_mfa, refresh and logout. Entries are keyed by
150        subject, not by session, so a re-authentication as a *different*
151        principal would otherwise read the previous principal's decisions.
152        """
153        with self._lock:
154            self._entries.clear()
155
156    def report_clamp(self, requested_ms: float, telemetry: TelemetryDispatcher) -> None:
157        """Emit a :class:`ConfigClamped` if the requested TTL was clamped (§19.2 rule 6).
158
159        This is the clamp that matters most to get right: an operator who set a
160        60-second TTL believes their staleness bound is 60 seconds. It is five,
161        and without this event nothing anywhere says so.
162
163        Nothing is emitted when the requested value was already inside the
164        limit, or when the memo is disabled — an event that fires when nothing
165        happened trains its reader to ignore it.
166        """
167        if not telemetry.installed or requested_ms <= 0.0 or requested_ms == self._ttl_ms:
168            return
169        telemetry.emit(
170            ConfigClamped(
171                setting="decision_memo_ttl_ms",
172                requested=str(requested_ms),
173                effective=str(self._ttl_ms),
174                contract_reference="§17.1 rule 2",
175            )
176        )
177
178    def __len__(self) -> int:
179        """Number of live entries, for tests."""
180        with self._lock:
181            return len(self._entries)

A bounded, TTL-clamped decision memo.

ttl_ms == 0 means disabled — not "cache for zero milliseconds". That is the default, and both get() and set() become no-ops.

Thread-safe: the sync client is commonly shared across a thread pool, and a cache that corrupted under concurrency would be a worse bug than the one it is optimising away.

Emit a ConfigClamped if the requested TTL was clamped (§19.2 rule 6).

This is the clamp that matters most to get right: an operator who set a 60-second TTL believes their staleness bound is 60 seconds. It is five, and without this event nothing anywhere says so.

Nothing is emitted when the requested value was already inside the limit, or when the memo is disabled — an event that fires when nothing happened trains its reader to ignore it.

TelemetryHook = collections.abc.Callable[[RequestStart | RequestEnd | Retry | Refresh | axiam_sdk._telemetry.ConfigClamped], None]

class AxiamClient(axiam_sdk._client._AxiamClientBase, axiam_sdk.management.ops.ManagementNamespaces): 
 711class AxiamClient(_AxiamClientBase, ManagementNamespaces):
 712    """The AXIAM SDK's sync REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10).
 713
 714    ``client.login(...)`` returns a typed :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult`
 715    with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1). For the async twin, use
 716    :class:`~axiam_sdk.AsyncAxiamClient` (SDK-Q08) — a separate class, not an
 717    ``async_*`` method on this one.
 718    """
 719
 720    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 721    # Lifecycle (D-19)
 722    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 723
 724    def __enter__(self) -> AxiamClient:
 725        """Context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no separate
 726        setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
 727        return self
 728
 729    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
 730        """Context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`close`, regardless of
 731        whether the ``with`` block raised (D-19)."""
 732        self.close()
 733
 734    def close(self) -> None:
 735        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
 736
 737        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
 738        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
 739
 740        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
 741        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
 742        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
 743        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
 744        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
 745        ending the session is what you want.
 746
 747        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
 748        rather than silently reconnecting.
 749        """
 750        self._closed = True
 751        self._decision_memo.clear()
 752        self._session.close()
 753
 754    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 755    # login / verify_mfa
 756    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 757
 758    def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 759        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
 760        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
 761        session is established (SC#1)."""
 762        self._ensure_open()
 763        self._on_credential_change()
 764        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 765            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
 766        )
 767        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 768        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 769
 770    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 771        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
 772
 773        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
 774        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
 775
 776        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
 777        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
 778        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
 779        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
 780        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
 781        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
 782        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
 783
 784        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
 785        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
 786        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
 787        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
 788        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
 789        nothing to skip.
 790
 791        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
 792            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
 793            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
 794            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
 795            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
 796            :meth:`login`.
 797        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
 798            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
 799            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
 800            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
 801
 802        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
 803        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
 804        ``opaque_mode``:
 805
 806        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
 807          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
 808          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
 809          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
 810          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
 811          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
 812          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
 813          to serve.
 814        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
 815          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
 816          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
 817          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
 818          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
 819
 820        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
 821        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
 822        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
 823        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
 824        credential.
 825
 826        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
 827        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
 828        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
 829        someone holding the OPRF seed.
 830        """
 831        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
 832
 833        self._ensure_open()
 834        self._on_credential_change()
 835
 836        exchange = start_login(password)
 837
 838        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
 839        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
 840        # not depend on the KSF.
 841        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 842            "POST",
 843            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
 844            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
 845        )
 846        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 847        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 848            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
 849        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
 850
 851        try:
 852            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
 853        except AuthError:
 854            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
 855            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
 856            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
 857                raise
 858            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
 859
 860        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 861            "POST",
 862            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
 863            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
 864        )
 865        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 866        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
 867            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
 868        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 869
 870    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 871        """Build a registration record sealed against the tenant this client is
 872        **acting on**.
 873
 874        That is the right tenant when the record is for an account being created
 875        in it — §27 ``users.create``, and the reset-completion flow, which names
 876        its own tenant. It is the **wrong** tenant for the caller's own password
 877        change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to
 878        act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use
 879        :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.
 880
 881        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
 882        arrive with the request or not at all.
 883
 884        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
 885        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
 886        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
 887        record.
 888
 889        Note the absence of an ``identity`` argument. The SRP version required
 890        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
 891        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
 892        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
 893
 894        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
 895            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
 896            SDK cannot perform.
 897        """
 898        return self._enroll(password, None)
 899
 900    def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 901        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
 902        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
 903
 904        CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. ``POST /auth/password/change`` and the record
 905        that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the
 906        client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting
 907        tenant is refused with *"the OPAQUE session was issued for a different
 908        tenant"*.
 909
 910        The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has
 911        selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are
 912        the same value and this behaves identically to
 913        :meth:`opaque_enrollment`. It is still the method to call for a
 914        self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is
 915        not something the call site usually knows.
 916
 917        :raises NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet —
 918            the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is
 919            nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as
 920            :meth:`opaque_enrollment` otherwise.
 921        """
 922        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
 923            raise NetworkError(
 924                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
 925                "building a registration record for your own password"
 926            )
 927        return self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)
 928
 929    def _enroll(self, password: str, principal_tenant_id: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
 930        """The shared body of the two enrolment methods; they differ only in the
 931        tenant the record is sealed against."""
 932        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
 933
 934        self._ensure_open()
 935        exchange = start_registration(password)
 936
 937        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 938            "POST",
 939            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
 940            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request, principal_tenant_id),
 941        )
 942        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 943        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 944            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
 945        started = response.json()
 946
 947        return {
 948            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
 949            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
 950                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
 951            ),
 952        }
 953
 954    def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
 955        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
 956        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
 957        true."""
 958        self._ensure_open()
 959        self._on_credential_change()
 960        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 961            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
 962        )
 963        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 964        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 965
 966    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 967    # refresh
 968    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 969
 970    def refresh(self) -> None:
 971        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
 972        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
 973        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
 974        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
 975        self._ensure_open()
 976        self._on_credential_change()
 977        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
 978        if not observed_access:
 979            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
 980
 981        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
 982        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
 983        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
 984        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
 985        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
 986            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
 987        )
 988
 989    def _do_refresh_sync(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 990        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
 991        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
 992        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_sync`
 993        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
 994        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
 995        one in-flight call (§9)."""
 996        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
 997        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
 998        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 999            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
1000        )
1001        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1002        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
1003
1004    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1005    # logout
1006    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1007
1008    def logout(self) -> None:
1009        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
1010        self._ensure_open()
1011        self._on_credential_change()
1012        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
1013        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1014            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
1015        )
1016        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1017        if response.status_code >= 300:
1018            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
1019        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
1020
1021    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1022    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check (Task 3)
1023    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1024
1025    def check_access(
1026        self,
1027        action: str,
1028        resource_id: str,
1029        scope: str | None = None,
1030        *,
1031        subject_id: str | None = None,
1032    ) -> AccessResult:
1033        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
1034
1035        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
1036        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
1037        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
1038        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
1039        *request's* authenticated user.
1040        """
1041        self._ensure_open()
1042        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
1043        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
1044        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1045        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
1046        if memoized is not None:
1047            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
1048            return memoized
1049
1050        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1051        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
1052        result = AccessResult(**wire)
1053
1054        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
1055        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
1056        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
1057        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
1058        return result
1059
1060    def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
1061        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
1062        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
1063        return self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope).allowed
1064
1065    def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
1066        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
1067        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
1068        self._ensure_open()
1069        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
1070        wire = self._authz_post_sync(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
1071        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
1072
1073    def _authz_post_sync(
1074        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
1075    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1076        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
1077
1078        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
1079        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
1080        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
1081        operation this policy covers.
1082
1083        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
1084        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
1085        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
1086        transport-failure budget would make sense.
1087        """
1088        return retry_sync(
1089            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_sync_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
1090            operation=operation,
1091            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
1092            telemetry=self._telemetry,
1093        )
1094
1095    def _authz_post_sync_once(
1096        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
1097    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1098        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
1099        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1100        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
1101            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1102
1103            if response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED:
1104                response = self._retry_after_refresh_sync(request)
1105
1106            span.status = response.status_code
1107            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
1108                raise error_from_http_status(
1109                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
1110                )
1111            span.outcome = "success"
1112            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
1113            return result
1114
1115    def _retry_after_refresh_sync(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
1116        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
1117        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
1118        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
1119        retry loop)."""
1120        self.refresh()
1121        retry_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1122            original_request.method,
1123            original_request.url,
1124            content=original_request.content,
1125            headers={
1126                k: v
1127                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
1128                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
1129            },
1130        )
1131        return self._session._send_sync(retry_request)
1132
1133    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1134    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3)
1135    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1136
1137    def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
1138        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1139        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
1140        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
1141        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
1142
1143        def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
1144            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
1145            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
1146            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
1147            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1148            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
1149
1150        return self._discovery_cache.get_sync(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
1151
1152    def oidc_begin(
1153        self,
1154        *,
1155        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
1156        redirect_uri: str,
1157        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1158        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
1159    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
1160        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
1161        local computation, no network I/O**. Nothing is stored: persist
1162        the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and ``code_verifier`` yourself
1163        (§12.3 rule 1)."""
1164        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
1165            configuration=configuration,
1166            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1167            scope=scope,
1168            extra_params=extra_params,
1169        )
1170
1171    def oidc_par(
1172        self,
1173        *,
1174        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1175        redirect_uri: str,
1176        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1177        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1178        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1179    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1180        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1181        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1182        with.
1183
1184        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1185        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1186        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1187        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1188        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1189        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1190
1191        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1192        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1193        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1194
1195        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1196        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1197
1198        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1199        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1200        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1201        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1202
1203        Raises:
1204            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1205                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1206            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1207        """
1208        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1209        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
1210        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1211        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1212        response = self._session._send_sync(http_request)
1213        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
1214
1215    def oidc_exchange(
1216        self,
1217        *,
1218        code: str,
1219        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
1220        redirect_uri: str,
1221        nonce: str,
1222        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1223        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1224    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1225        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
1226        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
1227        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
1228        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
1229        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
1230        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
1231        returned."""
1232        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1233        form = self._exchange_form(
1234            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
1235        )
1236        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1237        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1238        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1239        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
1240
1241    def oidc_refresh(
1242        self,
1243        *,
1244        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1245        scope: str | None = None,
1246        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1247        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1248    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1249        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1250        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1251
1252        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1253        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1254        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1255        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1256        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1257        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1258        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1259        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1260        interleave.
1261        """
1262
1263        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1264            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1265            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1266            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1267            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1268            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1269            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1270            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1271            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1272            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1273            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1274            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1275
1276        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1277            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1278            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1279            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1280            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1281            return token_set
1282
1283        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1284        return result
1285
1286    def login_client_credentials(
1287        self,
1288        *,
1289        scope: str | None = None,
1290        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1291        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1292    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1293        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
1294        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
1295        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
1296        ``id_token``.
1297
1298        Raises:
1299            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
1300                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
1301        """
1302        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1303        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
1304        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1305        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1306        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1307        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
1308        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1309
1310    def device_authorize(
1311        self,
1312        *,
1313        scope: str | None = None,
1314        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1315        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1316    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
1317        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
1318        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
1319
1320        **Unauthenticated by design.** A device that cannot show a browser
1321        also cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends
1322        ``client_secret`` and never refuses a client built without one.
1323
1324        Raises:
1325            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1326                ``device_authorization_endpoint``.
1327        """
1328        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1329        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
1330        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
1331        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1332        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1333        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1334            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
1335                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
1336            )
1337        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
1338
1339    def device_poll(
1340        self,
1341        *,
1342        device_code: SecretStr | str,
1343        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1344        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1345    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1346        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
1347        poll attempt.
1348
1349        The raw single call, so an application driving its own loop (a UI
1350        rendering a countdown, say) can. The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers
1351        surface as ``OAuthProtocolError`` — ``authorization_pending`` and
1352        ``slow_down`` included — so a hand-rolled loop sees exactly what
1353        :meth:`device_login` sees. Most callers want :meth:`device_login`.
1354        """
1355        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1356        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
1357        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1358        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1359        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1360        # No nonce: the device grant has no authorization request to carry one.
1361        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1362
1363    def device_login(
1364        self,
1365        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None],
1366        *,
1367        scope: str | None = None,
1368        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1369        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1370    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1371        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
1372        user code, poll to completion.
1373
1374        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1375        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1376        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1377        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1378        panel) is the application's decision.
1379
1380        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1381        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1382        posture.
1383
1384        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1385        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1386        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1387        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1388        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1389        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1390        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1391        user has already approved.
1392        """
1393        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1394        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1395            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1396        )
1397
1398        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1399        on_user_code(authorization)
1400
1401        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1402        while True:
1403            if not schedule.tick():
1404                raise self._device_expired_error()
1405            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1406            try:
1407                return self.device_poll(
1408                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1409                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1410                    configuration=config,
1411                )
1412            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1413                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1414                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1415                    continue
1416                if outcome == "slow_down":
1417                    schedule.slow_down()
1418                    continue
1419                raise
1420
1421    def token_exchange(
1422        self,
1423        *,
1424        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
1425        subject_token_type: str,
1426        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
1427        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1428        audience: str | None = None,
1429        resource: str | None = None,
1430        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1431        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1432    ) -> ExchangedToken:
1433        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1)
1434        — exchange a token for a **narrower** one.
1435
1436        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1437
1438        * **No default ``actor_token``** (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for
1439          *impersonation*; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own
1440          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
1441        * **No retry or downgrade on ``unauthorized_client``** (rule 2) — a
1442          registration fact an operator must fix.
1443        * **No auto-narrowing on ``invalid_scope``** (rule 3). The server
1444          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1445          out here.
1446        * **No adoption** (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one
1447          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1448          subsequent call this client makes.
1449
1450        A cross-tenant subject token answers ``invalid_grant``, identically to
1451        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1452        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1453        tenant-enumeration signal.
1454
1455        Args:
1456            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1457                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1458                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1459                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1460                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1461                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1462                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1463                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1464                a refusal as a different type.
1465
1466        Raises:
1467            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1468                with no wire call.
1469        """
1470        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1471        form = self._token_exchange_form(
1472            subject_token=subject_token,
1473            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1474            actor_token=actor_token,
1475            scopes=scopes,
1476            audience=audience,
1477            resource=resource,
1478        )
1479        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1480        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1481        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1482        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)
1483
1484    def uma_register_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet) -> ResourceSet:
1485        """``POST /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — register a resource set
1486        (CONTRACT.md §20.1).
1487
1488        The returned ``id`` **is** the AXIAM resource id, directly usable as
1489        the ``resource_id`` of a later :meth:`uma_request_ticket`.
1490        """
1491        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1492            "POST",
1493            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/rreg/resource_set"),
1494            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
1495            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1496        )
1497        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1498        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource registration failed")
1499        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)
1500
1501    def uma_read_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str) -> ResourceSet:
1502        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — read a resource set (§20.1)."""
1503        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1504            "GET",
1505            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1506            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1507        )
1508        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1509        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource read failed")
1510        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)
1511
1512    def uma_update_resource(
1513        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str, resource: ResourceSet
1514    ) -> ResourceSet:
1515        """``PUT /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — replace a resource set (§20.1).
1516
1517        **The scope list is replaced, not merged** (§20.2 rule 8). Whatever
1518        ``resource.resource_scopes`` holds becomes the complete declared set;
1519        omitting a scope removes it, which is how a resource server drops an
1520        authority. This method performs no read-before-write.
1521        """
1522        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1523            "PUT",
1524            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1525            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
1526            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1527        )
1528        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1529        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource update failed")
1530        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)
1531
1532    def uma_delete_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str) -> None:
1533        """``DELETE /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — deregister (§20.1)."""
1534        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1535            "DELETE",
1536            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1537            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1538        )
1539        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1540        self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource delete failed")

1542    def uma_list_resources(self, pat: SecretStr | str) -> list[str]:
1543        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — list the ids **this client**
1544        registered (§20.1).
1545
1546        Not the tenant's whole resource tree: a protection scope does not
1547        entitle a caller to enumerate it.
1548        """
1549        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1550            "GET",
1551            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/rreg/resource_set"),
1552            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1553        )
1554        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1555        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource list failed")
1556        return cast("list[str]", wire or [])

1558    def uma_request_ticket(
1559        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
1560    ) -> SecretStr:
1561        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
1562
1563        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
1564        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
1565        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
1566        server draws rather than flattening it.
1567        """
1568        body = [
1569            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
1570            for p in permissions
1571        ]
1572        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1573            "POST",
1574            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
1575            json=body,
1576            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1577        )
1578        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1579        wire = cast(
1580            "dict[str, str]",
1581            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
1582        )
1583        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])
1584
1585    def uma_exchange_ticket(
1586        self,
1587        *,
1588        ticket: SecretStr | str,
1589        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
1590        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1591        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1592    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
1593        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
1594        a ticket for an RPT.
1595
1596        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
1597        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
1598        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
1599        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
1600        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
1601        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
1602        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
1603        **new** ticket.
1604
1605        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1606
1607        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
1608          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
1609          resource server instead of for the user.
1610        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
1611          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
1612          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
1613        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
1614          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
1615          that user.
1616
1617        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
1618        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
1619        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
1620        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
1621
1622        Raises:
1623            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1624                with no wire call.
1625        """
1626        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1627        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
1628        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1629        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1630        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1631        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
1632
1633    def logout_url(
1634        self,
1635        *,
1636        id_token: SecretStr | str,
1637        post_logout_redirect_uri: str | None = None,
1638        state: str | None = None,
1639        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1640    ) -> str:
1641        """Build the RP-initiated logout URL to redirect the user agent to
1642        (CONTRACT.md §12.7.2).
1643
1644        Performs **no network I/O** beyond the discovery fetch the SDK caches
1645        anyway, and does **not** clear this client's own session: whether the
1646        local session ends is the application's decision — a backend holding a
1647        service-account session must not lose it because a *user* logged out.
1648
1649        ``end_session_endpoint`` is read from discovery and never synthesised
1650        from the issuer (rule 1). ``post_logout_redirect_uri`` is passed
1651        through unvalidated against any local list (rule 3): the allow-list
1652        lives in the client's server-side registration, and a client-side copy
1653        would drift and reject a URI an operator had just registered.
1654
1655        ``state`` is the caller's to generate and the caller's to check; the
1656        SDK never invents one, because the value only means something to the
1657        application that will receive it back.
1658        """
1659        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1660        return self._logout_url_impl(
1661            config,
1662            id_token=id_token,
1663            post_logout_redirect_uri=post_logout_redirect_uri,
1664            state=state,
1665        )
1666
1667    def verify_logout_token(
1668        self,
1669        token: str,
1670        *,
1671        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1672    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
1673        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
1674        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
1675
1676        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
1677
1678        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
1679           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
1680           ``kid``-required discipline.
1681        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
1682        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
1683           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
1684           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
1685        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
1686           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
1687           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
1688        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
1689           identifies nothing.
1690        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
1691
1692        Returns:
1693            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
1694            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
1695            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
1696            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
1697            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
1698            logout after a restart.
1699        """
1700        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1701        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)
1702
1703    def introspect(
1704        self,
1705        *,
1706        token: SecretStr | str,
1707        token_type_hint: str | None = None,
1708        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1709        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1710    ) -> IntrospectionResult:
1711        """``POST /oauth2/introspect`` (RFC 7662, CONTRACT.md §12.1) — ask
1712        the server whether a token is active and, if so, for its metadata.
1713        Requires confidential-client credentials (§12.1 note 4). A ``401``
1714        here is a client-credential failure surfaced as
1715        ``OAuthProtocolError``; it never enters the §9 single-flight
1716        refresh guard (a client-credential failure is not a session
1717        expiry)."""
1718        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1719        form = self._introspect_form(token=token, token_type_hint=token_type_hint)
1720        url = self._endpoint_url_for_introspect(config, tenant_id)
1721        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1722        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1723        return self._handle_introspect_response(response)
1724
1725    def revoke(
1726        self,
1727        *,
1728        token: SecretStr | str,
1729        token_type_hint: str | None = None,
1730        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1731        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1732    ) -> None:
1733        """``POST /oauth2/revoke`` (RFC 7009, CONTRACT.md §12.1) — revoke
1734        an access or refresh token. Idempotent: any ``200`` (including for
1735        a token the server has never seen) is success (§12.1 note 5); only
1736        a ``401`` (client authentication failed) is an error."""
1737        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1738        form = self._revoke_form(token=token, token_type_hint=token_type_hint)
1739        url = self._endpoint_url_for_revoke(config, tenant_id)
1740        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1741        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1742        self._handle_revoke_response(response)
