1744    def sso_start(
1745        self,
1746        *,
1747        federation_config_id: str,
1748        redirect_uri: str,
1749        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1750        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1751        org_id: str | None = None,
1752        org_slug: str | None = None,
1753    ) -> SsoStartResult:
1754        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/start`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1)
1755        — step 1 of first-time SSO against an upstream IdP. One tenant
1756        form and one org form must be resolvable, from the arguments or
1757        from the client's construction-time/resolved context (§5.1)."""
1758        body = self._sso_start_body(
1759            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
1760            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1761            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1762            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1763            org_id=org_id,
1764            org_slug=org_slug,
1765        )
1766        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", SSO_START_PATH, json=body)
1767        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1768        return self._handle_sso_start_response(response)
1769
1770    def sso_complete(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1771        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1772        §12.1) — step 2 of upstream SSO: consumes the single-use ``state``,
1773        provisions or links the user, and establishes the session via
1774        ``Set-Cookie`` (§4 cookie jar). §12.4 does not apply here — no ID
1775        token ever reaches the SDK on the federation path."""
1776        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1777            "POST", SSO_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1778        )
1779        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1780        return self._handle_sso_complete_response(response)
1781
1782    def sso_providers(
1783        self,
1784        *,
1785        org_id: str | None = None,
1786        org_slug: str | None = None,
1787        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1788        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1789    ) -> FederationProviderList:
1790        """``GET /api/v1/auth/federation/providers`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1791        which "Sign in with X" buttons to render for a workspace.
1792
1793        The identifiers travel as **query** parameters; this is a ``GET``
1794        and sends no body.
1795
1796        **An empty list is a success.** An unknown organization, a known one
1797        with nothing configured, and a request naming no workspace at all
1798        all answer ``200`` with an empty ``providers`` array (§12.1 note 9).
1799        Every one of them comes back as an ordinary result, and nothing here
1800        synthesises a not-found: the endpoint is deliberately shaped so it
1801        cannot be used to enumerate organization or tenant slugs, and an SDK
1802        that reintroduced the distinction would reintroduce the oracle. A
1803        caller learns it named the workspace wrongly at the start
1804        operations, where every failure is a uniform ``401``.
1805
1806        For the same reason this is the one federation operation that does
1807        **not** refuse client-side when no workspace resolves.
1808        """
1809        params = self._sso_providers_params(
1810            org_id=org_id,
1811            org_slug=org_slug,
1812            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1813            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1814        )
1815        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("GET", SSO_PROVIDERS_PATH, params=params)
1816        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1817        return self._handle_sso_providers_response(response)
1818
1819    def sso_start_oauth2(
1820        self,
1821        *,
1822        federation_config_id: str,
1823        redirect_uri: str,
1824        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1825        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1826        org_id: str | None = None,
1827        org_slug: str | None = None,
1828    ) -> SsoStartResult:
1829        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start`` (CONTRACT.md
1830        §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a **plain-OAuth2** upstream
1831        (GitHub, Facebook, ``generic_oauth2``).
1832
1833        Call this, rather than :meth:`sso_start`, exactly when the
1834        provider's ``protocol`` is ``OAuth2`` (§12.1 note 10). The server
1835        refuses a mismatch with ``400`` rather than accepting it silently,
1836        so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.
1837
1838        PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored
1839        **server-side**; nothing about it appears in the request or the
1840        response (§12.1 note 11).
1841
1842        A ``400`` here can mean the ``redirect_uri`` is not on an origin the
1843        deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as
1844        :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` and is not retried.
1845        """
1846        body = self._sso_start_oauth2_body(
1847            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
1848            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1849            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1850            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1851            org_id=org_id,
1852            org_slug=org_slug,
1853        )
1854        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", SSO_OAUTH2_START_PATH, json=body)
1855        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1856        return self._handle_sso_start_oauth2_response(response)
1857
1858    def sso_complete_oauth2(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1859        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1860        §12.1) — step 2 of a plain-OAuth2 login.
1861
1862        The session arrives as ``Set-Cookie`` (§12.1 note 6) and is absorbed
1863        exactly as :meth:`sso_complete` absorbs it, so ``refresh()`` and
1864        ``logout()`` work afterwards.
1865
1866        §12.4 does not apply: an ``OAuth2`` provider issues no ID token, so
1867        there is nothing to validate. The server authenticated the user by
1868        calling a configured userinfo endpoint with the access token it had
1869        just received — configuration and transport trust rather than
1870        cryptographic trust (§12.1 note 11).
1871        """
1872        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1873            "POST", SSO_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1874        )
1875        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1876        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteOauth2")
1877
1878    def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1879        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1880        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
1881
1882        Those two protocols return **cross-site**, so the server cannot set
1883        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
1884        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
1885        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
1886        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
1887        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
1888
1889        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
1890        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
1891        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
1892        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
1893        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
1894        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
1895        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
1896        do.
1897        """
1898        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1899            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
1900        )
1901        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1902        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")
1903
1904    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1905    # §24 WebAuthn / passkeys — the relying-party layer
1906    #
1907    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
1908    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
1909    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
1910    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
1911    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
1912    # a handset ran.
1913    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1914
1915    def webauthn_register_start(self) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1916        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1917
1918        Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user
1919        does to their own account — and refuses **client-side with no wire
1920        call** when there is none.
1921
1922        A ``503`` means the tenant's attestation policy requires attestation
1923        and the FIDO metadata service has no usable snapshot. That is a server
1924        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2
1925        deliberately does **not** retry it.
1926        """
1927        self._ensure_open()
1928        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")
1929        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._WA_REGISTER_START, json={})
1930        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1931        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_register_start")
1932
1933    def webauthn_register_finish(
1934        self,
1935        *,
1936        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1937        credential_name: str,
1938        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1939    ) -> WebauthnCredential:
1940        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1941
1942        ``response`` is either the parsed authenticator answer or the
1943        platform's own JSON string (§24.6a rule 2) — Android's
1944        ``registrationResponseJson``, a browser's ``credential.toJSON()``. It
1945        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a
1946        signature check over bytes this SDK did not produce.
1947        """
1948        self._ensure_open()
1949        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_finish")
1950        body = self._webauthn_register_finish_body(state_token, credential_name, response)
1951        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1952            "POST", self._WA_REGISTER_FINISH, json=body
1953        )
1954        return self._webauthn_credential(self._session._send_sync(request))
1955
1956    def webauthn_authenticate_start(self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1957        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1958
1959        The **second-factor** ceremony: it continues a ``login()`` that
1960        answered ``mfa_required`` with ``"webauthn"`` among its methods, and
1961        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.
1962
1963        A different flow from :meth:`webauthn_discoverable_start`, not the same
1964        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be
1965        merged.
1966        """
1967        self._ensure_open()
1968        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1969            "POST", self._WA_AUTH_START, json={"challenge_token": _expose_token(challenge_token)}
1970        )
1971        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1972        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_authenticate_start")
1973
1974    def webauthn_authenticate_finish(
1975        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1976    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1977        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1978
1979        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3 rule 1). That is not §14.3's
1980        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
1981        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —
1982        returning a token set without adopting it would make a passkey sign-in
1983        the one way to log in that does not log you in.
1984        """
1985        return self._webauthn_finish_sync(
1986            self._WA_AUTH_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_authenticate_finish"
1987        )
1988
1989    def webauthn_discoverable_start(
1990        self, *, workspace: WebauthnWorkspace | None = None
1991    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1992        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1993
1994        The **primary-factor** ceremony: nothing precedes it, the server sends
1995        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
1996        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential
1997        is resolved inside one tenant — but it comes from this client's own
1998        configuration unless overridden, and slugs are accepted.
1999        """
2000        self._ensure_open()
2001        body = self._webauthn_discoverable_body(workspace)
2002        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2003            "POST", self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_START, json=body
2004        )
2005        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
2006        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_discoverable_start")
2007
2008    def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
2009        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
2010    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
2011        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2012
2013        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
2014        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
2015        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.
2016        """
2017        return self._webauthn_finish_sync(
2018            self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_discoverable_finish"
2019        )
2020
2021    def _webauthn_finish_sync(
2022        self,
2023        path: str,
2024        state_token: SecretStr | str,
2025        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
2026        operation: str,
2027    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
2028        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
2029        self._ensure_open()
2030        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
2031        # this call changes the subject.
2032        self._on_credential_change()
2033        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
2034        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
2035        http_response = self._session._send_sync(request)
2036        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
2037        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
2038        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
2039        self._absorb_session_cookies()
2040        return result
2041
2042    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2043    # §25 Account lifecycle and MFA enrolment
2044    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2045
2046    def mfa_enroll(self) -> MfaEnrollment:
2047        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
2048        voluntary TOTP enrolment for the signed-in user.
2049
2050        Changes nothing about the current session. In particular it does
2051        **not** clear the §17 decision memo: the subject has not changed, and
2052        discarding a warm memo on an unrelated profile action costs a round
2053        trip on every check that follows (§25.2 rule 3).
2054        """
2055        self._ensure_open()
2056        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_MFA_ENROLL, json={})
2057        return self._mfa_enrollment(self._session._send_sync(request), "mfa_enroll")
2058
2059    def mfa_confirm(self, *, totp_code: str) -> bool:
2060        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — activate the
2061        factor :meth:`mfa_enroll` offered."""
2062        self._ensure_open()
2063        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2064            "POST", self._AC_MFA_CONFIRM, json={"totp_code": totp_code}
2065        )
2066        return self._mfa_confirmed(self._session._send_sync(request))
2067
2068    def mfa_setup_enroll(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> MfaEnrollment:
2069        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
2070        the enrolment a ``login()`` demanded.
2071
2072        Reached when ``login()`` returns ``mfa_setup_required``: the tenant
2073        requires MFA and this account has none. There is no session yet — the
2074        setup token *is* the credential.
2075        """
2076        self._ensure_open()
2077        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2078            "POST", self._AC_MFA_SETUP_ENROLL, json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token)}
2079        )
2080        return self._mfa_enrollment(self._session._send_sync(request), "mfa_setup_enroll")
2081
2082    def mfa_setup_confirm(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str, totp_code: str) -> LoginResult:
2083        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — finish
2084        forced enrolment and, with it, the login that was interrupted.
2085
2086        Adopts credentials exactly as ``login()`` does, because it *is* the
2087        completion of a login (§25.2 rule 2).
2088        """
2089        self._ensure_open()
2090        self._on_credential_change()
2091        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2092            "POST",
2093            self._AC_MFA_SETUP_CONFIRM,
2094            json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token), "totp_code": totp_code},
2095        )
2096        return self._handle_login_response(self._session._send_sync(request))
2097
2098    def verify_email(self, *, token: SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
2099        """``POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1).
2100
2101        Unauthenticated: a user whose address is unverified may have no session
2102        at all. ``tenant_id`` is a **body** field here — this is not an
2103        ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint, so §12.1 rule 2's query-parameter convention
2104        does not reach it.
2105        """
2106        self._ensure_open()
2107        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2108            "POST",
2109            self._AC_VERIFY_EMAIL,
2110            json={"token": _expose_token(token), "tenant_id": tenant_id},
2111        )
2112        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "verify_email")
2113
2114    def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
2115        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
2116        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
2117
2118        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
2119        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
2120        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
2121        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
2122        accounts (§25.7).
2123
2124        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
2125        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
2126        is the name you already knew.
2127        """
2128        self._ensure_open()
2129        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2130            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
2131        )
2132        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "resend_verification")
2133
2134    def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
2135        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
2136        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
2137        and say what happened.
2138
2139        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
2140        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
2141        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
2142        address.
2143
2144        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
2145        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
2146        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
2147
2148        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
2149          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
2150          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
2151          succeeding.
2152        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
2153          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
2154        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
2155
2156        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
2157        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
2158        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
2159        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
2160        """
2161        self._ensure_open()
2162        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2163            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
2164        )
2165        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "resend_own_verification")
2166
2167    def request_password_reset(
2168        self,
2169        *,
2170        email: str,
2171        org_slug: str | None = None,
2172        tenant_id: str | None = None,
2173        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
2174    ) -> None:
2175        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — ask for a reset
2176        mail.
2177
2178        **Returns normally whether or not the address exists**, and this SDK
2179        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
2180        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
2181        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
2182        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).
2183        """
2184        self._ensure_open()
2185        body = self._password_reset_body(
2186            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
2187        )
2188        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_RESET, json=body)
2189        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "request_password_reset")

def close(self) -> None: 
734    def close(self) -> None:
735        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
736
737        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
738        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
739
740        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
741        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
742        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
743        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
744        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
745        ending the session is what you want.
746
747        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
748        rather than silently reconnecting.
749        """
750        self._closed = True
751        self._decision_memo.clear()
752        self._session.close()

def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
770    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
771        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
772
773        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
774        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
775
776        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
777        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
778        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
779        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
780        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
781        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
782        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
783
784        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
785        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
786        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
787        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
788        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
789        nothing to skip.
790
791        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
792            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
793            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
794            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
795            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
796            :meth:`login`.
797        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
798            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
799            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
800            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
801
802        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
803        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
804        ``opaque_mode``:
805
806        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
807          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
808          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
809          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
810          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
811          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
812          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
813          to serve.
814        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
815          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
816          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
817          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
818          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
819
820        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
821        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
822        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
823        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
824        credential.
825
826        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
827        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
828        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
829        someone holding the OPRF seed.
830        """
831        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
832
833        self._ensure_open()
834        self._on_credential_change()
835
836        exchange = start_login(password)
837
838        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
839        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
840        # not depend on the KSF.
841        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
842            "POST",
843            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
844            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
845        )
846        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
847        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
848            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
849        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
850
851        try:
852            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
853        except AuthError:
854            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
855            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
856            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
857                raise
858            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
859
860        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
861            "POST",
862            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
863            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
864        )
865        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
866        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
867            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
868        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.

What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither useful without the account's registration record and the tenant's OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password, because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not offer. It does not protect against a compromised AXIAM server.

Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the server during the handshake, so opening KE2 is the proof that it holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an M2 check in capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now nothing to skip.

Raises
  • NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not AuthError: reporting a configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to login().
  • AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist, an account with no registration record, and a server that does not hold the record — indistinguishable by design. Nothing is sent to login/finish in that case (§23.4 rule 7).

The mode field decides what happens after a failed exchange, and nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). login/start carries the tenant's opaque_mode:

  • "optional" — this method retries over login() with the same credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's outcome. Under optional an account with no record is the ordinary case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state optional exists to serve.
  • "required", an unrecognised value, or no mode at all (a server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is retried over login(). It would be refused anyway: required answers 403 opaque_required for every principal in the tenant, so trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.

mode is not downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer 404 and get the fallback whatever it puts here. required is what closes that, server-side, by refusing /auth/login before examining any credential.

This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by someone holding the OPRF seed.

def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
870    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
871        """Build a registration record sealed against the tenant this client is
872        **acting on**.
873
874        That is the right tenant when the record is for an account being created
875        in it — §27 ``users.create``, and the reset-completion flow, which names
876        its own tenant. It is the **wrong** tenant for the caller's own password
877        change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to
878        act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use
879        :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.
880
881        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
882        arrive with the request or not at all.
883
884        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
885        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
886        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
887        record.
888
889        Note the absence of an ``identity`` argument. The SRP version required
890        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
891        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
892        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
893
894        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
895            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
896            SDK cannot perform.
897        """
898        return self._enroll(password, None)

Build a registration record sealed against the tenant this client is acting on.

That is the right tenant when the record is for an account being created in it — §27 users.create, and the reset-completion flow, which names its own tenant. It is the wrong tenant for the caller's own password change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use opaque_enrollment_for_self() there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.

The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to arrive with the request or not at all.

Performs a register/start round trip, which the SRP verifier this replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid record.

Note the absence of an identity argument. The SRP version required the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.

Raises

def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
900    def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
901        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
902        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
903
904        CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. ``POST /auth/password/change`` and the record
905        that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the
906        client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting
907        tenant is refused with *"the OPAQUE session was issued for a different
908        tenant"*.
909
910        The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has
911        selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are
912        the same value and this behaves identically to
913        :meth:`opaque_enrollment`. It is still the method to call for a
914        self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is
915        not something the call site usually knows.
916
917        :raises NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet —
918            the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is
919            nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as
920            :meth:`opaque_enrollment` otherwise.
921        """
922        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
923            raise NetworkError(
924                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
925                "building a registration record for your own password"
926            )
927        return self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)

Build a registration record for the caller's own new password, sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.

CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. POST /auth/password/change and the record that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting tenant is refused with "the OPAQUE session was issued for a different tenant".

The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are the same value and this behaves identically to opaque_enrollment(). It is still the method to call for a self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is not something the call site usually knows.

Raises
  • NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet — the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as opaque_enrollment() otherwise.

970    def refresh(self) -> None:
971        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
972        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
973        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
974        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
975        self._ensure_open()
976        self._on_credential_change()
977        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
978        if not observed_access:
979            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
980
981        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
982        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
983        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
984        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
985        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
986            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
987        )

def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
1025    def check_access(
1026        self,
1027        action: str,
1028        resource_id: str,
1029        scope: str | None = None,
1030        *,
1031        subject_id: str | None = None,
1032    ) -> AccessResult:
1033        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
1034
1035        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
1036        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
1037        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
1038        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
1039        *request's* authenticated user.
1040        """
1041        self._ensure_open()
1042        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
1043        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
1044        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1045        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
1046        if memoized is not None:
1047            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
1048            return memoized
1049
1050        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1051        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
1052        result = AccessResult(**wire)
1053
1054        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
1055        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
1056        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
1057        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
1058        return result

1171    def oidc_par(
1172        self,
1173        *,
1174        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1175        redirect_uri: str,
1176        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1177        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1178        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1179    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1180        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1181        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1182        with.
1183
1184        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1185        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1186        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1187        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1188        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1189        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1190
1191        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1192        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1193        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1194
1195        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1196        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1197
1198        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1199        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1200        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1201        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1202
1203        Raises:
1204            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1205                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1206            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1207        """
1208        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1209        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
1210        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1211        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1212        response = self._session._send_sync(http_request)
1213        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

POST /oauth2/par (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect with.

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

A §12 extension, not a replacement: oidc_exchange afterwards is unchanged, and takes the code_verifier carried on the result.

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

1235        )

def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
1241    def oidc_refresh(
1242        self,
1243        *,
1244        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1245        scope: str | None = None,
1246        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1247        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1248    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1249        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1250        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1251
1252        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1253        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1254        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1255        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1256        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1257        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1258        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1259        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1260        interleave.
1261        """
1262
1263        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1264            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1265            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1266            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1267            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1268            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1269            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1270            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1271            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1272            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1273            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1274            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1275
1276        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1277            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1278            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1279            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1280            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1281            return token_set
1282
1283        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1284        return result

POST /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an OidcTokenSet.

A distinct operation from refresh(), which drives the cookie/opaque-token session path at POST /api/v1/auth/refresh (§12.1 "oidc_refresh vs refresh") — the two are never merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent oidc_refresh calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9 single-flight guard the cookie-session refresh() uses, so an oidc_refresh and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never interleave.

The raw single call, so an application driving its own loop (a UI rendering a countdown, say) can. def device_login( self, on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None], *, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
1363    def device_login(
1364        self,
1365        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None],
1366        *,
1367        scope: str | None = None,
1368        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1369        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1370    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1371        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
1372        user code, poll to completion.
1373
1374        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1375        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1376        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1377        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1378        panel) is the application's decision.
1379
1380        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1381        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1382        posture.
1383
1384        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1385        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1386        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1387        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1388        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1389        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1390        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1391        user has already approved.
1392        """
1393        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1394        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1395            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1396        )
1397
1398        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1399        on_user_code(authorization)
1400
1401        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1402        while True:
1403            if not schedule.tick():
1404                raise self._device_expired_error()
1405            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1406            try:
1407                return self.device_poll(
1408                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1409                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1410                    configuration=config,
1411                )
1412            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1413                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1414                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1415                    continue
1416                if outcome == "slow_down":
1417                    schedule.slow_down()
1418                    continue
1419                raise

The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the user code, poll to completion.

on_user_code is called with the DeviceAuthorization before the first poll — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink panel) is the application's decision.

Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK returns the token set rather than adopting it, matching its login_client_credentials posture.

Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response; slow_down adds 5 s permanently; authorization_pending loops; access_denied and expired_token raise distinct errors; polling stops at expires_in even if the server has not yet said expired_token. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is not terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the user has already approved.

def token_exchange( self, *, subject_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, subject_token_type: str, actor_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str | None = None, scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None, audience: str | None = None, resource: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> ExchangedToken: 
1421    def token_exchange(
1422        self,
1423        *,
1424        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
1425        subject_token_type: str,
1426        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
1427        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1428        audience: str | None = None,
1429        resource: str | None = None,
1430        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1431        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1432    ) -> ExchangedToken:
1433        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1)
1434        — exchange a token for a **narrower** one.
1435
1436        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1437
1438        * **No default ``actor_token``** (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for
1439          *impersonation*; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own
1440          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
1441        * **No retry or downgrade on ``unauthorized_client``** (rule 2) — a
1442          registration fact an operator must fix.
1443        * **No auto-narrowing on ``invalid_scope``** (rule 3). The server
1444          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1445          out here.
1446        * **No adoption** (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one
1447          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1448          subsequent call this client makes.
1449
1450        A cross-tenant subject token answers ``invalid_grant``, identically to
1451        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1452        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1453        tenant-enumeration signal.
1454
1455        Args:
1456            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1457                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1458                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1459                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1460                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1461                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1462                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1463                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1464                a refusal as a different type.
1465
1466        Raises:
1467            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1468                with no wire call.
1469        """
1470        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1471        form = self._token_exchange_form(
1472            subject_token=subject_token,
1473            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1474            actor_token=actor_token,
1475            scopes=scopes,
1476            audience=audience,
1477            resource=resource,
1478        )
1479        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1480        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1481        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1482        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1) — exchange a token for a narrower one.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default actor_token (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for impersonation; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
  • No retry or downgrade on unauthorized_client (rule 2) — a registration fact an operator must fix.
  • No auto-narrowing on invalid_scope (rule 3). The server refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds out here.
  • No adoption (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every subsequent call this client makes.

A cross-tenant subject token answers invalid_grant, identically to an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the server collapses them because distinguishing them is a tenant-enumeration signal.

Args: subject_token_type: What kind of token subject_token is. None sends ~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE, the same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a trusted external issuer (§15.7), set this explicitly — normally to ~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE. The SDK never reads subject_token to decide the value: which kind of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry a refusal as a different type.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

def uma_request_ticket( self, pat: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]) -> pydantic.types.SecretStr: 
1558    def uma_request_ticket(
1559        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
1560    ) -> SecretStr:
1561        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
1562
1563        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
1564        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
1565        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
1566        server draws rather than flattening it.
1567        """
1568        body = [
1569            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
1570            for p in permissions
1571        ]
1572        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1573            "POST",
1574            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
1575            json=body,
1576            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1577        )
1578        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1579        wire = cast(
1580            "dict[str, str]",
1581            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
1582        )
1583        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])

Scope names are validated here, against each resource's declared set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a 400, not a denial — the two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the server draws rather than flattening it.

1586        self,

1593        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
1594        a ticket for an RPT.

1596        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
1597        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
1598        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
1599        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
1600        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
1601        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
1602        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
1603        **new** ticket.
1604
1605        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1606
1607        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
1608          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
1609          resource server instead of for the user.
1610        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
1611          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
1612          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
1613        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
1614          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
1615          that user.
1616
1617        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
1618        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
1619        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
1620        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
1621
1622        Raises:
1623            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1624                with no wire call.
1625        """
1626        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1627        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
1628        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1629        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1630        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1631        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a ticket for an RPT.

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

def verify_logout_token( self, token: str, *, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> VerifiedLogoutToken: 
1667    def verify_logout_token(
1668        self,
1669        token: str,
1670        *,
1671        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1672    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
1673        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
1674        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
1675
1676        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
1677
1678        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
1679           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
1680           ``kid``-required discipline.
1681        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
1682        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
1683           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
1684           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
1685        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
1686           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
1687           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
1688        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
1689           identifies nothing.
1690        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
1691
1692        Returns:
1693            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
1694            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
1695            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
1696            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
1697            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
1698            logout after a restart.
1699        """
1700        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1701        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)

Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this application's backchannel_logout_uri (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).

Every check exists because skipping it has a name:

  1. Signature, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same kid-required discipline.
  2. iss/aud: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
  3. events carries the back-channel-logout key. This is what distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
  4. nonce is absent. Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it, and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
  5. At least one of sid/sub — a token naming neither identifies nothing.
  6. exp in the future, iat recent.

Returns: The sid/sub/jti the token names — never a bare bool, because the RP has to know which session to end. Dedup on jti yourself: delivery is at-least-once, so a valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second logout after a restart.

1920        call** when there is none.

Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user does to their own account — and refuses client-side with no wire call when there is none.

def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:

2136        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,

2145        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the

2149          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
2150          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
2151          succeeding.

2153          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
2154        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
2155
2156        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
2157        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
2158        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
2159        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
2160        """
2161        self._ensure_open()
2162        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(

2164        )

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
