class AsyncAxiamClient(axiam_sdk._client._AxiamClientBase, axiam_sdk.management.ops.AsyncManagementNamespaces): 
  86class AsyncAxiamClient(_AxiamClientBase, AsyncManagementNamespaces):
  87    """The AXIAM SDK's dedicated async REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10,
  88    SDK-Q08).
  89
  90    ``await client.login(...)`` returns a typed
  91    :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult` with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1) — the
  92    same contract as the sync :class:`~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient`, on its own
  93    dedicated async object. Constructing both an ``AxiamClient`` and an
  94    ``AsyncAxiamClient`` against the same ``base_url``/``tenant_slug`` gives
  95    each its own independent ``_Session`` (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh
  96    guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only
  97    each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.
  98    """
  99
 100    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 101    # Lifecycle (D-19)
 102    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 103
 104    async def __aenter__(self) -> AsyncAxiamClient:
 105        """Async context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no
 106        separate setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
 107        return self
 108
 109    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
 110        """Async context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`aclose`,
 111        regardless of whether the ``async with`` block raised (D-19)."""
 112        await self.aclose()
 113
 114    async def aclose(self) -> None:
 115        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
 116
 117        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
 118        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
 119
 120        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
 121        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
 122        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
 123        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
 124        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
 125        ending the session is what you want.
 126
 127        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
 128        rather than silently reconnecting.
 129        """
 130        self._closed = True
 131        self._decision_memo.clear()
 132        await self._session.aclose()
 133
 134    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 135    # login / verify_mfa
 136    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 137
 138    async def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 139        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
 140        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
 141        session is established (SC#1)."""
 142        self._ensure_open()
 143        self._on_credential_change()
 144        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 145            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
 146        )
 147        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 148        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 149
 150    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 151        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
 152
 153        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
 154        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
 155        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
 156        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
 157        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
 158        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
 159        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
 160        ``mfa_required`` case.
 161
 162        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
 163        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
 164        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
 165        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
 166        """
 167        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
 168
 169        self._ensure_open()
 170        self._on_credential_change()
 171
 172        exchange = start_login(password)
 173
 174        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 175            "POST",
 176            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
 177            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
 178        )
 179        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 180        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 181            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
 182        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
 183
 184        try:
 185            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
 186        except AuthError:
 187            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
 188            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
 189            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
 190                raise
 191            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
 192
 193        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 194            "POST",
 195            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
 196            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
 197        )
 198        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 199        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
 200            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
 201        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 202
 203    async def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 204        """Build a registration record for *password*, sealed against the tenant
 205        this client is **acting on**.
 206
 207        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment`; see that method
 208        for the full contract, including why the caller's *own* password change
 209        wants :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` instead.
 210        """
 211        return await self._enroll(password, None)
 212
 213    async def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 214        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
 215        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
 216
 217        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment_for_self`; see
 218        that method for the full contract (CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2).
 219        """
 220        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
 221            raise NetworkError(
 222                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
 223                "building a registration record for your own password"
 224            )
 225        return await self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)
 226
 227    async def _enroll(self, password: str, principal_tenant_id: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
 228        """The shared body of the two enrolment methods; they differ only in the
 229        tenant the record is sealed against."""
 230        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
 231
 232        self._ensure_open()
 233        exchange = start_registration(password)
 234
 235        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 236            "POST",
 237            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
 238            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request, principal_tenant_id),
 239        )
 240        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 241        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 242            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
 243        started = response.json()
 244
 245        return {
 246            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
 247            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
 248                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
 249            ),
 250        }
 251
 252    async def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
 253        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
 254        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
 255        true."""
 256        self._ensure_open()
 257        self._on_credential_change()
 258        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 259            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
 260        )
 261        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 262        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 263
 264    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 265    # refresh — exactly one literal /api/v1/auth/refresh POST, routed
 266    # through the single-flight guard (Pitfall 4, §9.3)
 267    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 268
 269    async def refresh(self) -> None:
 270        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
 271        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
 272        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
 273        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
 274        self._ensure_open()
 275        self._on_credential_change()
 276        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
 277        if not observed_access:
 278            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
 279
 280        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
 281        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
 282        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
 283        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
 284        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
 285            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
 286        )
 287
 288    async def _do_refresh_async(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 289        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
 290        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
 291        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_async`
 292        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
 293        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
 294        one in-flight call (§9)."""
 295        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
 296        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
 297        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 298            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
 299        )
 300        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 301        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
 302
 303    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 304    # logout
 305    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 306
 307    async def logout(self) -> None:
 308        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
 309        self._ensure_open()
 310        self._on_credential_change()
 311        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
 312        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 313            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
 314        )
 315        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 316        if response.status_code >= 300:
 317            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
 318        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
 319
 320    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 321    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check
 322    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 323
 324    async def check_access(
 325        self,
 326        action: str,
 327        resource_id: str,
 328        scope: str | None = None,
 329        *,
 330        subject_id: str | None = None,
 331    ) -> AccessResult:
 332        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
 333
 334        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
 335        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
 336        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
 337        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
 338        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
 339        (often service-account) session.
 340        """
 341        self._ensure_open()
 342        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
 343        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
 344        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 345        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
 346        if memoized is not None:
 347            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
 348            return memoized
 349
 350        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 351        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
 352        result = AccessResult(**wire)
 353
 354        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
 355        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
 356        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
 357        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
 358        return result
 359
 360    async def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
 361        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
 362        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
 363        result = await self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope)
 364        return result.allowed
 365
 366    async def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
 367        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
 368        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
 369        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
 370        wire = await self._authz_post_async(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
 371        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
 372
 373    async def _authz_post_async(
 374        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
 375    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 376        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
 377
 378        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
 379        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
 380        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
 381        operation this policy covers.
 382
 383        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
 384        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
 385        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
 386        transport-failure budget would make sense.
 387        """
 388        return await retry_async(
 389            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_async_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
 390            operation=operation,
 391            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
 392            telemetry=self._telemetry,
 393        )
 394
 395    async def _authz_post_async_once(
 396        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
 397    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 398        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
 399        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
 400        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
 401            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 402
 403            if response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED:
 404                response = await self._retry_after_refresh_async(request)
 405
 406            span.status = response.status_code
 407            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
 408                raise error_from_http_status(
 409                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
 410                )
 411            span.outcome = "success"
 412            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
 413            return result
 414
 415    async def _retry_after_refresh_async(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
 416        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
 417        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
 418        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
 419        retry loop)."""
 420        await self.refresh()
 421        retry_request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 422            original_request.method,
 423            original_request.url,
 424            content=original_request.content,
 425            headers={
 426                k: v
 427                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
 428                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
 429            },
 430        )
 431        return await self._session._send_async(retry_request)
 432
 433    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 434    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3, SDK-Q08)
 435    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 436
 437    async def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
 438        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
 439        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
 440        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
 441        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
 442
 443        async def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
 444            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
 445            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
 446            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
 447            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 448            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
 449
 450        return await self._discovery_cache.get_async(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
 451
 452    async def oidc_begin(
 453        self,
 454        *,
 455        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
 456        redirect_uri: str,
 457        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 458        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
 459    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
 460        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
 461        local computation, no network I/O**; this ``async def`` has no
 462        internal ``await`` (CONTRACT.md §12.2's Python naming table gives
 463        ``oidc_begin`` no synchronous carve-out the way it does for C#).
 464        Nothing is stored: persist the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and
 465        ``code_verifier`` yourself (§12.3 rule 1)."""
 466        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
 467            configuration=configuration,
 468            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
 469            scope=scope,
 470            extra_params=extra_params,
 471        )
 472
 473    async def oidc_par(
 474        self,
 475        *,
 476        request: AuthorizationRequest,
 477        redirect_uri: str,
 478        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 479        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 480        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 481    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
 482        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
 483        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
 484        with.
 485
 486        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
 487        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
 488        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
 489        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
 490        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
 491        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
 492
 493        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
 494        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
 495        authorize any other way (§21.1).
 496
 497        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
 498        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
 499
 500        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
 501        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
 502        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
 503        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
 504
 505        Raises:
 506            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
 507                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
 508            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
 509        """
 510        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 511        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
 512        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
 513        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 514        response = await self._session._send_async(http_request)
 515        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
 516
 517    async def oidc_exchange(
 518        self,
 519        *,
 520        code: str,
 521        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
 522        redirect_uri: str,
 523        nonce: str,
 524        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 525        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 526    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 527        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
 528        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
 529        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
 530        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
 531        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
 532        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
 533        returned."""
 534        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 535        form = self._exchange_form(
 536            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
 537        )
 538        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 539        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 540        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 541        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
 542
 543    async def oidc_refresh(
 544        self,
 545        *,
 546        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
 547        scope: str | None = None,
 548        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 549        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 550    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 551        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
 552        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
 553
 554        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
 555        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
 556        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
 557        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
 558        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
 559        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
 560        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
 561        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
 562        interleave.
 563        """
 564
 565        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
 566            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
 567            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
 568            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
 569            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
 570            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 571            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
 572            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 573            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 574            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 575            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
 576            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 577
 578        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
 579            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
 580            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
 581            :meth:`refresh` call."""
 582            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
 583                do_refresh
 584            )
 585            return token_set
 586
 587        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
 588        return result
 589
 590    async def login_client_credentials(
 591        self,
 592        *,
 593        scope: str | None = None,
 594        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 595        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 596    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 597        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
 598        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
 599        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
 600        ``id_token``.
 601
 602        Raises:
 603            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
 604                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
 605        """
 606        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 607        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
 608        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 609        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 610        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 611        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
 612        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 613
 614    async def device_authorize(
 615        self,
 616        *,
 617        scope: str | None = None,
 618        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 619        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 620    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
 621        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
 622        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
 623
 624        **Unauthenticated by design**: a device that cannot show a browser also
 625        cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends ``client_secret`` and
 626        never refuses a client built without one.
 627
 628        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.device_authorize`; §14.4
 629        requires the same three names on both clients.
 630        """
 631        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 632        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
 633        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
 634        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 635        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 636        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 637            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
 638                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
 639            )
 640        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
 641
 642    async def device_poll(
 643        self,
 644        *,
 645        device_code: SecretStr | str,
 646        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 647        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 648    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 649        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
 650        poll attempt.
 651
 652        The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers surface as ``OAuthProtocolError``,
 653        ``authorization_pending`` and ``slow_down`` included, so a hand-rolled
 654        loop sees exactly what :meth:`device_login` sees.
 655        """
 656        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 657        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
 658        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 659        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 660        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 661        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 662
 663    async def device_login(
 664        self,
 665        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
 666        *,
 667        scope: str | None = None,
 668        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 669        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 670    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 671        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
 672        user code, poll to completion.
 673
 674        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
 675        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
 676        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
 677        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
 678
 679        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
 680        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
 681        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
 682        """
 683        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 684        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
 685            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
 686        )
 687
 688        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
 689        result = on_user_code(authorization)
 690        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
 691            await result
 692
 693        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
 694        while True:
 695            if not schedule.tick():
 696                raise self._device_expired_error()
 697            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
 698            try:
 699                return await self.device_poll(
 700                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
 701                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
 702                    configuration=config,
 703                )
 704            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
 705                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
 706                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
 707                    continue
 708                if outcome == "slow_down":
 709                    schedule.slow_down()
 710                    continue
 711                raise
 712
 713    async def token_exchange(
 714        self,
 715        *,
 716        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
 717        subject_token_type: str,
 718        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
 719        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
 720        audience: str | None = None,
 721        resource: str | None = None,
 722        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 723        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 724    ) -> ExchangedToken:
 725        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (§15.1) — exchange a
 726        token for a **narrower** one.
 727
 728        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.token_exchange`; see that
 729        docstring for what this method deliberately refuses to do (no
 730        defaulted ``actor_token``, no auto-narrowing, no adoption) and for
 731        ``subject_token_type``, which reaches the external exchange of §15.7
 732        and is never inferred from the token.
 733        """
 734        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 735        form = self._token_exchange_form(
 736            subject_token=subject_token,
 737            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
 738            actor_token=actor_token,
 739            scopes=scopes,
 740            audience=audience,
 741            resource=resource,
 742        )
 743        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 744        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 745        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 746        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)

 749        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet

 778    async def uma_update_resource(
 779        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str, resource: ResourceSet
 780    ) -> ResourceSet:
 781        """``PUT /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — replace a resource set (§20.1).

 784        ``resource.resource_scopes`` holds becomes the complete declared set;
 785        omitting a scope removes it, which is how a resource server drops an
 786        authority. This method performs no read-before-write.
 787        """

 789            "PUT",
 790            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),

 793        )
 794        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 795        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource update failed")
 796        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

 824    async def uma_request_ticket(
 825        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
 826    ) -> SecretStr:
 827        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
 828
 829        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
 830        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
 831        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
 832        server draws rather than flattening it.
 833        """
 834        body = [
 835            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
 836            for p in permissions
 837        ]
 838        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 839            "POST",
 840            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
 841            json=body,
 842            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 843        )
 844        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 845        wire = cast(
 846            "dict[str, str]",
 847            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
 848        )
 849        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])

 851    async def uma_exchange_ticket(
 852        self,
 853        *,
 854        ticket: SecretStr | str,
 855        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
 856        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 857        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 858    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
 859        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.
 860
 861        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
 862        ticket for an RPT.
 863
 864        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
 865        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
 866        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
 867        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
 868        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
 869        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
 870        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
 871        failure, request a **new** ticket.
 872
 873        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
 874
 875        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
 876          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
 877          resource server instead of for the user.
 878        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
 879          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
 880          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
 881        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
 882          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
 883          that user.
 884
 885        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
 886        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
 887        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
 888        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
 889
 890        Raises:
 891            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
 892                with no wire call.
 893        """
 894        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 895        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
 896        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 897        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 898        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 899        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
 900

 989        — step 1 of first-time SSO against an upstream IdP. One tenant
 990        form and one org form must be resolvable, from the arguments or
 991        from the client's construction-time/resolved context (§5.1)."""

1004    async def sso_complete(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1005        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1006        §12.1) — step 2 of upstream SSO: consumes the single-use ``state``,
1007        provisions or links the user, and establishes the session via
1008        ``Set-Cookie`` (§4 cookie jar). §12.4 does not apply here — no ID
1009        token ever reaches the SDK on the federation path."""

1011            "POST", SSO_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1012        )

1014        return self._handle_sso_complete_response(response)

1016    async def sso_providers(
1017        self,
1018        *,
1019        org_id: str | None = None,
1020        org_slug: str | None = None,
1021        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1022        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1023    ) -> FederationProviderList:
1024        """``GET /api/v1/auth/federation/providers`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1025        which "Sign in with X" buttons to render for a workspace.
1026
1027        The identifiers travel as **query** parameters; this is a ``GET``
1028        and sends no body.
1029
1030        **An empty list is a success.** An unknown organization, a known one
1031        with nothing configured, and a request naming no workspace at all
1032        all answer ``200`` with an empty ``providers`` array (§12.1 note 9).
1033        Every one of them comes back as an ordinary result, and nothing here
1034        synthesises a not-found: the endpoint is deliberately shaped so it
1035        cannot be used to enumerate organization or tenant slugs, and an SDK
1036        that reintroduced the distinction would reintroduce the oracle. A
1037        caller learns it named the workspace wrongly at the start
1038        operations, where every failure is a uniform ``401``.
1039
1040        For the same reason this is the one federation operation that does
1041        **not** refuse client-side when no workspace resolves.
1042        """
1043        params = self._sso_providers_params(
1044            org_id=org_id,
1045            org_slug=org_slug,
1046            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1047            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1048        )
1049        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("GET", SSO_PROVIDERS_PATH, params=params)
1050        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1051        return self._handle_sso_providers_response(response)
1052
1053    async def sso_start_oauth2(
1054        self,
1055        *,
1056        federation_config_id: str,
1057        redirect_uri: str,
1058        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1059        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1060        org_id: str | None = None,
1061        org_slug: str | None = None,
1062    ) -> SsoStartResult:
1063        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start`` (CONTRACT.md
1064        §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a **plain-OAuth2** upstream
1065        (GitHub, Facebook, ``generic_oauth2``).
1066
1067        Call this, rather than :meth:`sso_start`, exactly when the
1068        provider's ``protocol`` is ``OAuth2`` (§12.1 note 10). The server
1069        refuses a mismatch with ``400`` rather than accepting it silently,
1070        so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.
1071
1072        PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored
1073        **server-side**; nothing about it appears in the request or the
1074        response (§12.1 note 11).
1075
1076        A ``400`` here can mean the ``redirect_uri`` is not on an origin the
1077        deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as
1078        :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` and is not retried.
1079        """
1080        body = self._sso_start_oauth2_body(
1081            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
1082            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1083            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1084            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1085            org_id=org_id,
1086            org_slug=org_slug,
1087        )
1088        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", SSO_OAUTH2_START_PATH, json=body)
1089        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1090        return self._handle_sso_start_oauth2_response(response)
1091
1092    async def sso_complete_oauth2(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1093        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1094        §12.1) — step 2 of a plain-OAuth2 login.
1095
1096        The session arrives as ``Set-Cookie`` (§12.1 note 6) and is absorbed
1097        exactly as :meth:`sso_complete` absorbs it, so ``refresh()`` and
1098        ``logout()`` work afterwards.
1099
1100        §12.4 does not apply: an ``OAuth2`` provider issues no ID token, so
1101        there is nothing to validate. The server authenticated the user by
1102        calling a configured userinfo endpoint with the access token it had
1103        just received — configuration and transport trust rather than
1104        cryptographic trust (§12.1 note 11).
1105        """
1106        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1107            "POST", SSO_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1108        )
1109        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1110        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteOauth2")
1111
1112    async def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1113        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1114        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
1115
1116        Those two protocols return **cross-site**, so the server cannot set
1117        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
1118        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
1119        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
1120        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
1121        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
1122
1123        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
1124        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
1125        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
1126        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
1127        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
1128        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
1129        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
1130        do.
1131        """
1132        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1133            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
1134        )
1135        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1136        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")
1137
1138    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1139    # §24 WebAuthn / passkeys — the relying-party layer (async twins)
1140    #
1141    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
1142    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
1143    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
1144    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
1145    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
1146    # a handset ran.
1147    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1148
1149    async def webauthn_register_start(self) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1150        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1151
1152        Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user
1153        does to their own account — and refuses **client-side with no wire
1154        call** when there is none.
1155
1156        A ``503`` means the tenant's attestation policy requires attestation
1157        and the FIDO metadata service has no usable snapshot. That is a server
1158        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2
1159        deliberately does **not** retry it.
1160        """
1161        self._ensure_open()
1162        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")
1163        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._WA_REGISTER_START, json={})
1164        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1165        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_register_start")
1166
1167    async def webauthn_register_finish(
1168        self,
1169        *,
1170        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1171        credential_name: str,
1172        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1173    ) -> WebauthnCredential:
1174        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1175
1176        ``response`` is either the parsed authenticator answer or the
1177        platform's own JSON string (§24.6a rule 2) — Android's
1178        ``registrationResponseJson``, a browser's ``credential.toJSON()``. It
1179        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a
1180        signature check over bytes this SDK did not produce.
1181        """
1182        self._ensure_open()
1183        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_finish")
1184        body = self._webauthn_register_finish_body(state_token, credential_name, response)
1185        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1186            "POST", self._WA_REGISTER_FINISH, json=body
1187        )
1188        return self._webauthn_credential(await self._session._send_async(request))
1189
1190    async def webauthn_authenticate_start(
1191        self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str
1192    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1193        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1194
1195        The **second-factor** ceremony: it continues a ``login()`` that
1196        answered ``mfa_required`` with ``"webauthn"`` among its methods, and
1197        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.
1198
1199        A different flow from :meth:`webauthn_discoverable_start`, not the same
1200        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be
1201        merged.
1202        """
1203        self._ensure_open()
1204        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1205            "POST", self._WA_AUTH_START, json={"challenge_token": _expose_token(challenge_token)}
1206        )
1207        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1208        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_authenticate_start")
1209
1210    async def webauthn_authenticate_finish(
1211        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1212    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1213        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1214
1215        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3 rule 1). That is not §14.3's
1216        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
1217        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —
1218        returning a token set without adopting it would make a passkey sign-in
1219        the one way to log in that does not log you in.
1220        """
1221        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1222            self._WA_AUTH_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_authenticate_finish"
1223        )
1224
1225    async def webauthn_discoverable_start(
1226        self, *, workspace: WebauthnWorkspace | None = None
1227    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1228        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1229
1230        The **primary-factor** ceremony: nothing precedes it, the server sends
1231        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
1232        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential
1233        is resolved inside one tenant — but it comes from this client's own
1234        configuration unless overridden, and slugs are accepted.
1235        """
1236        self._ensure_open()
1237        body = self._webauthn_discoverable_body(workspace)
1238        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1239            "POST", self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_START, json=body
1240        )
1241        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1242        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_discoverable_start")
1243
1244    async def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
1245        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1246    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1247        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1248
1249        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
1250        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
1251        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.
1252        """
1253        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1254            self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_discoverable_finish"
1255        )
1256
1257    async def _webauthn_finish_async(
1258        self,
1259        path: str,
1260        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1261        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1262        operation: str,
1263    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1264        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
1265        self._ensure_open()
1266        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
1267        # this call changes the subject.
1268        self._on_credential_change()
1269        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
1270        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1271        http_response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1272        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
1273        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
1274        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
1275        self._absorb_session_cookies()
1276        return result
1277
1278    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1279    # §25 Account lifecycle and MFA enrolment (async twins)
1280    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1281
1282    async def mfa_enroll(self) -> MfaEnrollment:
1283        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1284        voluntary TOTP enrolment for the signed-in user.
1285
1286        Changes nothing about the current session. In particular it does
1287        **not** clear the §17 decision memo: the subject has not changed, and
1288        discarding a warm memo on an unrelated profile action costs a round
1289        trip on every check that follows (§25.2 rule 3).
1290        """
1291        self._ensure_open()
1292        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_MFA_ENROLL, json={})
1293        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._session._send_async(request), "mfa_enroll")
1294
1295    async def mfa_confirm(self, *, totp_code: str) -> bool:
1296        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — activate the
1297        factor :meth:`mfa_enroll` offered."""
1298        self._ensure_open()
1299        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1300            "POST", self._AC_MFA_CONFIRM, json={"totp_code": totp_code}
1301        )
1302        return self._mfa_confirmed(await self._session._send_async(request))
1303
1304    async def mfa_setup_enroll(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> MfaEnrollment:
1305        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1306        the enrolment a ``login()`` demanded.
1307
1308        Reached when ``login()`` returns ``mfa_setup_required``: the tenant
1309        requires MFA and this account has none. There is no session yet — the
1310        setup token *is* the credential.
1311        """
1312        self._ensure_open()
1313        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1314            "POST", self._AC_MFA_SETUP_ENROLL, json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token)}
1315        )
1316        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._session._send_async(request), "mfa_setup_enroll")
1317
1318    async def mfa_setup_confirm(
1319        self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str, totp_code: str
1320    ) -> LoginResult:
1321        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — finish
1322        forced enrolment and, with it, the login that was interrupted.
1323
1324        Adopts credentials exactly as ``login()`` does, because it *is* the
1325        completion of a login (§25.2 rule 2).
1326        """
1327        self._ensure_open()
1328        self._on_credential_change()
1329        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1330            "POST",
1331            self._AC_MFA_SETUP_CONFIRM,
1332            json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token), "totp_code": totp_code},
1333        )
1334        return self._handle_login_response(await self._session._send_async(request))

1336    async def verify_email(self, *, token: SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1337        """``POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1).
1338
1339        Unauthenticated: a user whose address is unverified may have no session
1340        at all. ``tenant_id`` is a **body** field here — this is not an
1341        ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint, so §12.1 rule 2's query-parameter convention
1342        does not reach it.
1343        """
1344        self._ensure_open()
1345        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1346            "POST",
1347            self._AC_VERIFY_EMAIL,
1348            json={"token": _expose_token(token), "tenant_id": tenant_id},
1349        )
1350        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "verify_email")
1351
1352    async def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1353        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
1354        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
1355
1356        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
1357        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
1358        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
1359        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
1360        accounts (§25.7).
1361
1362        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
1363        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
1364        is the name you already knew.
1365        """
1366        self._ensure_open()
1367        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1368            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
1369        )
1370        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_verification")
1371
1372    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1373        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1374        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1375        and say what happened.
1376
1377        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1378        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1379        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1380        address.
1381
1382        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1383        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1384        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1385
1386        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1387          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1388          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1389          succeeding.
1390        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1391          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1392        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1393
1394        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1395        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1396        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1397        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1398        """
1399        self._ensure_open()
1400        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1401            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1402        )
1403        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_own_verification")
1404
1405    async def request_password_reset(
1406        self,
1407        *,
1408        email: str,
1409        org_slug: str | None = None,
1410        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1411        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1412    ) -> None:
1413        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — ask for a reset
1414        mail.
1415
1416        **Returns normally whether or not the address exists**, and this SDK
1417        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
1418        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
1419        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
1420        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).
1421        """
1422        self._ensure_open()
1423        body = self._password_reset_body(
1424            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
1425        )
1426        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_RESET, json=body)
1427        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "request_password_reset")
1428
1429    async def password_reset_context(self, *, token: SecretStr | str) -> PasswordResetContext:
1430        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE
1431        policy for the account a reset token belongs to.
1432
1433        Call this before :meth:`confirm_password_reset` on any tenant that
1434        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,
1435        and building one needs parameters it cannot know before it has a token
1436        to ask with. Sending a plaintext password to a tenant in
1437        ``opaque_mode: required`` is refused, and refused late (§25.4 rule 1).
1438        """
1439        self._ensure_open()
1440        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1441            "GET", self._AC_RESET_CONTEXT, params={"token": _expose_token(token)}
1442        )
1443        return self._reset_context(await self._session._send_async(request))
1444
1445    async def confirm_password_reset(
1446        self,
1447        *,
1448        token: SecretStr | str,
1449        new_password: SecretStr | str,
1450        tenant_id: str,
1451        opaque: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
1452    ) -> None:
1453        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1)."""

1455        body = self._password_reset_confirm_body(
1456            token=token, new_password=new_password, tenant_id=tenant_id, opaque=opaque
1457        )
1458        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1459            "POST", self._AC_RESET_CONFIRM, json=body
1460        )
1461        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "confirm_password_reset")

The AXIAM SDK's dedicated async REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10, SDK-Q08).

await client.login(...) returns a typed ~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult with mfa_required (SC#1) — the same contract as the sync ~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient, on its own dedicated async object. Constructing both an AxiamClient and an AsyncAxiamClient against the same base_url/tenant_slug gives each its own independent _Session (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.

async def aclose(self) -> None: 
114    async def aclose(self) -> None:
115        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
116
117        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
118        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
119
120        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
121        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
122        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
123        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
124        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
125        ending the session is what you want.
126
127        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
128        rather than silently reconnecting.
129        """
130        self._closed = True
131        self._decision_memo.clear()
132        await self._session.aclose()

async def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
150    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
151        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
152
153        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
154        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
155        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
156        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
157        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
158        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
159        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
160        ``mfa_required`` case.
161
162        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
163        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
164        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
165        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
166        """
167        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
168
169        self._ensure_open()
170        self._on_credential_change()
171
172        exchange = start_login(password)
173
174        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
175            "POST",
176            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
177            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
178        )
179        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
180        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
181            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
182        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
183
184        try:
185            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
186        except AuthError:
187            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
188            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
189            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
190                raise
191            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
192
193        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
194            "POST",
195            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
196            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
197        )
198        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
199        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
200            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
201        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

The async twin of AxiamClient.login_opaque(); see that method for the full contract — including what the login/start response's mode field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under "optional" this retries over login() and returns that call's outcome, and under "required", an unrecognised value or no mode at all it raises AuthError and retries nothing. Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case.

The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in asyncio.to_thread().

async def refresh(self) -> None: 
269    async def refresh(self) -> None:
270        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
271        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
272        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
273        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
274        self._ensure_open()
275        self._on_credential_change()
276        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
277        if not observed_access:
278            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
279
280        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
281        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
282        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
283        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
284        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
285            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
286        )

async def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
324    async def check_access(
325        self,
326        action: str,
327        resource_id: str,
328        scope: str | None = None,
329        *,
330        subject_id: str | None = None,
331    ) -> AccessResult:
332        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
333
334        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
335        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
336        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
337        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
338        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
339        (often service-account) session.
340        """
341        self._ensure_open()
342        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
343        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
344        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
345        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
346        if memoized is not None:
347            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
348            return memoized
349
350        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
351        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
352        result = AccessResult(**wire)
353
354        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
355        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
356        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
357        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
358        return result

async def oidc_par( self, *, request: AuthorizationRequest, redirect_uri: str, scope: str | list[str] | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest: 
473    async def oidc_par(
474        self,
475        *,
476        request: AuthorizationRequest,
477        redirect_uri: str,
478        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
479        tenant_id: str | None = None,
480        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
481    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
482        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
483        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
484        with.
485
486        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
487        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
488        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
489        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
490        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
491        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
492
493        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
494        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
495        authorize any other way (§21.1).
496
497        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
498        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
499
500        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
501        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
502        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
503        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
504
505        Raises:
506            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
507                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
508            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
509        """
510        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
511        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
512        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
513        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
514        response = await self._session._send_async(http_request)
515        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

async def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
543    async def oidc_refresh(
544        self,
545        *,
546        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
547        scope: str | None = None,
548        tenant_id: str | None = None,
549        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
550    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
551        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
552        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
553
554        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
555        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
556        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
557        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
558        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
559        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
560        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
561        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
562        interleave.
563        """
564
565        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
566            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
567            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
568            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
569            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
570            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
571            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
572            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
573            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
574            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
575            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
576            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
577
578        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
579            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
580            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
581            :meth:`refresh` call."""
582            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
583                do_refresh
584            )
585            return token_set
586
587        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
588        return result

POST /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an OidcTokenSet.

A distinct operation from refresh(), which drives the cookie/opaque-token session path at POST /api/v1/auth/refresh (§12.1 "oidc_refresh vs refresh") — the two are never merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent oidc_refresh calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9 single-flight guard the cookie-session refresh() uses, so an oidc_refresh and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never interleave.
