async def device_login( self, on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]], *, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
663    async def device_login(
664        self,
665        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
666        *,
667        scope: str | None = None,
668        tenant_id: str | None = None,
669        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
670    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
671        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
672        user code, poll to completion.
673
674        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
675        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
676        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
677        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
678
679        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
680        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
681        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
682        """
683        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
684        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
685            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
686        )
687
688        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
689        result = on_user_code(authorization)
690        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
691            await result
692
693        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
694        while True:
695            if not schedule.tick():
696                raise self._device_expired_error()
697            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
698            try:
699                return await self.device_poll(
700                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
701                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
702                    configuration=config,
703                )
704            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
705                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
706                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
707                    continue
708                if outcome == "slow_down":
709                    schedule.slow_down()
710                    continue
711                raise

The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the user code, poll to completion.

on_user_code is invoked — and awaited when it returns an awaitable — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.

Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK returns the token set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync twin's docstring for the full rule set.

854        ticket: SecretStr | str,

859        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.

861        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
862        ticket for an RPT.

864        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
865        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
866        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
867        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
868        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
869        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
870        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
871        failure, request a **new** ticket.
872
873        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
874
875        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
876          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
877          resource server instead of for the user.
878        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
879          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
880          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
881        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
882          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
883          that user.
884
885        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client

887        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
888        cannot probe for live ticket handles.

892                with no wire call.

894        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
895        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
896        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
897        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
898        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
899        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a ticket for an RPT.

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

1125        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed

1128        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
1129        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
1130        do.

async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None: 
1372    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1373        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1374        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1375        and say what happened.
1376
1377        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1378        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1379        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1380        address.
1381
1382        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1383        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1384        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1385
1386        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1387          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1388          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1389          succeeding.
1390        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1391          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1392        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1393
1394        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1395        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1396        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1397        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1398        """
1399        self._ensure_open()
1400        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1401            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1402        )
1403        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_own_verification")

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.

 39    #: ``mfa_setup_enroll``, show the user the URI, then ``mfa_setup_confirm``,
 40    #: which completes this login.

 52    """Whether the account that just signed in is an **organization-level**
 53    principal — CONTRACT.md §5.2.
 54
 55    Such a principal's record lives in its organization's reserved tenant, so
 56    its global grants apply in every tenant of that organization, and it can act
 57    on a different one by sending a different ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` on the next
 58    request — no re-login, because it already is a principal of every tenant
 59    there.
 60
 61    An ordinary tenant principal is a principal of exactly one tenant. Changing
 62    the header for one of those produces a ``403``, so this flag is what an
 63    application checks *before* offering a tenant switch, rather than
 64    discovering the answer from a failed request.
 65

 67    and ``False`` on the two pending outcomes, where no principal has been
 68    established yet.

 71    alone no longer decides what to offer: consult
 72    :attr:`reachable_tenant_ids` as well (§5.2.3 rule 3).
 73    """

 77
 78    Distinct from the tenant a request *acts on*: the two are the same value for
 79    every ordinary principal and diverge only once an organization-level one
 80    selects another tenant.
 81
 82    This is where the account's own credentials belong, and what a §23
 83    registration record for *this* account must be sealed against — see
 84    ``AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment_for_self``.
 85
 86    Falls back to the acting tenant the server reported when it omits this,
 87    which is exactly right there: a server older than contract 1.34 cannot
 88    switch the acting tenant, so the two cannot differ.
 89    """
 90

 94    """

100    /api/v1/organizations``, which is ``super-admin``-only and returns only the
101    caller's own organization.
102    """
103
104    reachable_tenant_ids: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
105    """The tenants this caller's roles reach, when narrowed — CONTRACT.md
106    §5.2.3.
107
108    ``None`` means **unrestricted**, which is both the common case and the only

110    deliberately narrowed organization-level account: confine any tenant switch

112    rule 4).
113
114    Note the pairing with :attr:`organization_level`: a narrowed account still
115    reports ``True`` there, so gating on that flag alone offers tenants the
116    server will refuse.
117    """
118

Such a principal's record lives in its organization's reserved tenant, so its global grants apply in every tenant of that organization, and it can act on a different one by sending a different X-Axiam-Tenant on the next request — no re-login, because it already is a principal of every tenant there.

Read this rather than resolving a slug through GET /api/v1/organizations, which is super-admin-only and returns only the caller's own organization.

reachable_tenant_ids: tuple[str, ...] | None = None

The tenants this caller's roles reach, when narrowed — CONTRACT.md §5.2.3.

None means unrestricted, which is both the common case and the only thing a server older than contract 1.35 can mean. A present tuple is a deliberately narrowed organization-level account: confine any tenant switch to it, because naming anything outside is refused at the header (§5.2.3 rule 4).

Note the pairing with organization_level: a narrowed account still reports True there, so gating on that flag alone offers tenants the server will refuse.

205@dataclass(frozen=True)
206class UmaChallenger:
207    """A configured ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).
208
209    Hand one to :func:`axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access` (or Django's
210    ``@require_access``) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a
211    fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in
212    the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of
213    only being told "no".
214
215    **Opt-in, and deliberately so.** Emitting a challenge means minting a
216    credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced
217    on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on
218    every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a
219    Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your
220    own authorization server.
221
222    **Failure is not escalation.** If minting fails — the PAT expired, the
223    Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes —
224    the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller
225    who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API
226    outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence,
227    and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.
228
229    :param realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
230    :param as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally
231        this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated
232        by hand.
233    :param pat: A Protection API Token: a *client-credentials* token carrying
234        the ``uma_protection`` scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand
235        in — a minted ticket is bound to the ``client_id`` that minted it.
236    :param client: The client whose ``uma_request_ticket`` mints the ticket.
237        Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.
238    """
239
240    realm: str
241    as_uri: str
242    pat: SecretStr | str
243    client: Any

A configured WWW-Authenticate: UMA challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).

Hand one to axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access() (or Django's @require_access) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of only being told "no".

Opt-in, and deliberately so. Emitting a challenge means minting a credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your own authorization server.

Failure is not escalation. If minting fails — the PAT expired, the Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes — the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence, and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.

Parameters
  • realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
  • as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated by hand.
  • pat: A Protection API Token: a client-credentials token carrying the uma_protection scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand in — a minted ticket is bound to the client_id that minted it.
  • client: The client whose uma_request_ticket mints the ticket. Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.

def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None: 
161def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None:
162    """Parse a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA …`` header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).
163
164    **This deliberately does not exchange the ticket.** Parsing a challenge and
165    acting on it are separate decisions: the ``as_uri`` names an authorization
166    server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging
167    would send the requesting party's ``claim_token`` to whatever host answered
168    the 403. The caller decides.
169
170    Returns ``None`` when the header is not a UMA challenge.
171    """
172    trimmed = header.strip()
173    if not trimmed.startswith("UMA"):
174        return None
175    rest = trimmed[3:]
176    # "UMA" alone is a valid, if useless, challenge; anything else must be
177    # separated by whitespace so `UMAX realm="…"` is not read as UMA.
178    if rest and not rest[0].isspace():
179        return None
180
181    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
182    for part in rest.split(","):
183        key, sep, value = part.partition("=")
184        if not sep:
185            continue
186        fields[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip('"')
187
188    ticket = fields.get("ticket")
189    return UmaChallenge(
190        realm=fields.get("realm"),
191        as_uri=fields.get("as_uri"),
192        ticket=SecretStr(ticket) if ticket is not None else None,
193    )

Parse a WWW-Authenticate: UMA … header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).

This deliberately does not exchange the ticket. Parsing a challenge and acting on it are separate decisions: the as_uri names an authorization server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging would send the requesting party's claim_token to whatever host answered the 403. The caller decides.

Returns None when the header is not a UMA challenge.

def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str) -> str: 
196def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: SecretStr | str) -> str:
197    """Format a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` header value (§20.3, emit half).
198
199    The resource-server side: having obtained a ticket from
200    ``uma_request_ticket``, tell the caller where to redeem it.
201    """
202    return f'UMA realm="{realm}", as_uri="{as_uri}", ticket="{_expose_secret(ticket)}"'

class AuthError(builtins.Exception): 
30class AuthError(Exception):
31    """Authentication failure: wrong credentials, expired session, MFA
32    failure, or a 401 on refresh (CONTRACT.md §2)."""
33
34    def __init__(self, message: str, reason: str | None = None) -> None:
35        """Build the exception with ``message`` describing the failure
36        (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the exception's own ``str()``
37        prefixes it with ``"authentication failed: "``.
38
39        ``reason`` is an optional stable, machine-readable code (CONTRACT.md
40        §12.3 rule 3 / §12.4) — populated by the OIDC ID-token validation
41        checklist with one of the seven contract-fixed reason codes
42        (``invalid_alg``, ``unknown_kid``, ``invalid_signature``,
43        ``invalid_issuer``, ``invalid_audience``, ``token_expired``,
44        ``nonce_mismatch``); ``None`` for every other ``AuthError``. It is a
45        code, never free text, so callers can branch on it without parsing
46        ``message``.
47        """
48        super().__init__(f"authentication failed: {message}")
49        self.message = message

111class NetworkError(Exception):
112    """Transport-level failure: connection refused, timeout, TLS error, DNS

114
115    ``cause`` is set as ``__cause__`` for standard Python exception chaining
116    (``raise ... from cause`` semantics). It MUST only ever be populated via
117    ``error_from_http_status``/``error_from_grpc_status``, which redact
118    sensitive headers from any wrapped ``httpx.Response`` BEFORE constructing
119    this error (D-08, CR-04 carry-forward) — never construct this class
120    directly from an unredacted response.
121    """
122
123    def __init__(self, message: str, cause: BaseException | None = None) -> None:
124        """Build the exception with ``message`` and an optional already-
125        redacted ``cause`` (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the
126        exception's own ``str()`` prefixes ``message`` with ``"network
127        error: "``. See the class docstring for the redact-before-wrap
128        invariant governing ``cause``."""
129        super().__init__(f"network error: {message}")
130        self.message = message
131        self.__cause__ = cause

class OAuthProtocolError(axiam_sdk.AuthError): 
53class OAuthProtocolError(AuthError):
54    """An RFC 6749 protocol error returned by an ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint as an
55    ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` body (CONTRACT.md §2 sub-type table, §12.3 rule 3,
56    port-brief-addendum item 17).
57
58    A **sub-type of** :class:`AuthError`, not a fourth peer error type:
59    existing ``except AuthError:`` blocks keep matching it unchanged — that
60    backward compatibility is precisely what makes contract 1.4 "non-breaking,
61    additive". Raised for a ``400`` from ``POST /oauth2/token`` (e.g.
62    ``invalid_grant``) and for a ``401`` from ``POST /oauth2/introspect`` /
63    ``POST /oauth2/revoke`` (client authentication failed) — neither of which
64    may collapse into the generic §2 ``400 -> NetworkError`` / ``401 ->
65    AuthError`` rows.
66
67    ``str(exc)`` is always exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, built
68    from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire fields, which are also exposed
69    individually as :attr:`error`/:attr:`error_description`. This
70    deliberately bypasses :class:`AuthError`'s own ``"authentication failed:
71    "`` message-prefixing convention: §12.3 rule 3 fixes this class's message
72    to exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, so ``Exception.__init__``
73    is called directly rather than via ``AuthError.__init__``.
74    """
75
76    def __init__(self, error: str, error_description: str) -> None:
77        """Build the exception from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire
78        fields (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 3); ``error``/``error_description``
79        are exposed as public attributes, and ``str(self)`` is exactly
80        ``"<error>: <error_description>"``."""
81        message = f"{error}: {error_description}"
82        Exception.__init__(self, message)
83        self.message = message
84        self.reason = None
85        self.error = error
86        self.error_description = error_description

This is an unauthenticated response and carries only what a button needs. There is no client_id, no metadata_url, no endpoint URL and no secret — absent by construction rather than filtered out — and §12.1 note 9 forbids an SDK from expecting one.

id: str = PydanticUndefined

Config id, to be echoed back to the matching start operation.

Pass it through unmodified: inheritance is resolved server-side (§12.1 note 13) and this id is how the server is told what resolution produced.

provider_kind: str = PydanticUndefined

Which provider this is, for the button's branding — google, github, generic_oidc, … Not what selects the start operation; see protocol.

display_name: str = PydanticUndefined

The operator's display name for the provider.

protocol: str = PydanticUndefined

OidcConnect, Saml or OAuth2 — the value that selects which start operation to call (§12.1 note 10). Compare against PROTOCOL_OIDC_CONNECT/PROTOCOL_OAUTH2/PROTOCOL_SAML.

Kept as the wire string rather than narrowed to an enum: the server owns this vocabulary, and an SDK enum would turn a value added server-side into a validation failure for the whole list.

An OAuth2 provider issues no ID token — the server authenticates by calling a configured userinfo endpoint, so there is no signature, no nonce and no aud (§12.1 note 11). A surface rendering these buttons SHOULD make that distinction visible rather than presenting the two as equivalent.

has_bundled_mark: bool = PydanticUndefined

Whether AXIAM ships this provider's own sign-in mark, which its button must then use. False for the generic kinds, whose buttons read "Sign in with display_name" and use button_icon where the operator uploaded one.

inherited: bool = PydanticUndefined

True when the provider is inherited from the organization rather than configured on this tenant (§12.1 note 13). Informational — it is not needed to sign in, and nothing in this SDK computes it.

button_icon: str | None = None

The operator's uploaded button icon as a bounded raster data: URL. None for most providers: present only for generic ones whose operator uploaded a mark.

58class OidcStateStore(Protocol):
59    """Optional server-side store for in-flight ``oidc_begin`` state
60    (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).
61
62    Implement this to back the login/callback handlers with your own
63    storage (Redis, a database, an encrypted cookie). Two invariants are
64    normative:
65
66    1. **Single-use.** :meth:`consume` MUST return the entry *and delete it
67       atomically*, so a replayed callback cannot reuse a ``state``.
68    2. **Expiry.** An entry older than 10 minutes MUST NOT be returned.
69    """
70
71    def save(self, entry: OidcStateEntry) -> None:
72        """Persist ``entry``, keyed by its ``state``, starting its TTL now."""
73        ...
74
75    def consume(self, state: str) -> OidcStateEntry | None:
76        """Atomically fetch **and remove** the entry for ``state``.
77
78        Returns ``None`` when the state is unknown, already consumed, or
79        expired — three cases a caller MUST treat identically (as a failed
80        login), because distinguishing them leaks whether a ``state`` ever
81        existed.
82        """
83        ...

Implement this to back the login/callback handlers with your own storage (Redis, a database, an encrypted cookie). Two invariants are normative:

1771def _no_init_or_replace_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
1772    cls = type(self)
1773
1774    if cls._is_protocol:
1775        raise TypeError('Protocols cannot be instantiated')
1776
1777    # Already using a custom `__init__`. No need to calculate correct
1778    # `__init__` to call. This can lead to RecursionError. See bpo-45121.
1779    if cls.__init__ is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1780        return
1781
1782    # Initially, `__init__` of a protocol subclass is set to `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1783    # The first instantiation of the subclass will call `_no_init_or_replace_init` which
1784    # searches for a proper new `__init__` in the MRO. The new `__init__`
1785    # replaces the subclass' old `__init__` (ie `_no_init_or_replace_init`). Subsequent
1786    # instantiation of the protocol subclass will thus use the new
1787    # `__init__` and no longer call `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1788    for base in cls.__mro__:
1789        init = base.__dict__.get('__init__', _no_init_or_replace_init)
1790        if init is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1791            cls.__init__ = init
1792            break
1793    else:
1794        # should not happen
1795        cls.__init__ = object.__init__
1796
1797    cls.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)

class MemoryOidcStateStore: 
 86class MemoryOidcStateStore:
 87    """In-memory reference implementation of :class:`OidcStateStore`
 88    (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).
 89
 90    Per-instance (never process-global), single-use, 10-minute TTL. Expired
 91    entries are dropped lazily on :meth:`consume` and swept opportunistically
 92    on :meth:`save` — no background thread/timer is held, since a library
 93    must not keep the host process alive (port-brief-addendum item 8).
 94
 95    Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance
 96    deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement
 97    :class:`OidcStateStore` yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes
 98    this class.
 99
100    Thread-safe: guarded by a single ``threading.Lock`` so concurrent sync
101    and async (via ``asyncio``'s default single-threaded event loop, or a
102    thread-pool-offloaded call) callers never corrupt the underlying dict.
103    """
104
105    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS) -> None:
106        """Build an empty store.
107
108        Args:
109            ttl_seconds: Entry lifetime in seconds. Defaults to
110                :data:`OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS` (10 minutes) and is
111                **clamped to it**: a shorter TTL is honored (useful in
112                tests), a longer one is reduced, because CONTRACT.md §12.3
113                rule 1 fixes 10 minutes as the maximum.
114        """
115        self._ttl_seconds = min(ttl_seconds, OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS)
116        self._entries: dict[str, tuple[OidcStateEntry, float]] = {}
117        self._lock = threading.Lock()
118
119    @property
120    def size(self) -> int:
121        """Number of unexpired entries currently held (tests/metrics)."""
122        with self._lock:
123            self._sweep_locked()
124            return len(self._entries)
125
126    def save(self, entry: OidcStateEntry) -> None:
127        """Persist ``entry`` under its own ``state``, expiring
128        ``ttl_seconds`` from now."""
129        with self._lock:
130            self._sweep_locked()
131            self._entries[entry.state] = (entry, time.monotonic() + self._ttl_seconds)
132
133    def consume(self, state: str) -> OidcStateEntry | None:
134        """Atomically return and delete the entry for ``state``.
135
136        Deletion happens before the expiry check, so even an expired hit is
137        removed rather than left to accumulate, and a second call can never
138        return the same entry twice.
139        """
140        with self._lock:
141            held = self._entries.pop(state, None)
142            if held is None:
143                return None
144            entry, expires_at = held
145            if expires_at <= time.monotonic():
146                return None
147            return entry
148
149    def _sweep_locked(self) -> None:
150        """Drop every expired entry. Caller MUST already hold ``self._lock``.
151        Lazy housekeeping — no background timer."""
152        now = time.monotonic()
153        expired = [
154            state for state, (_entry, expires_at) in self._entries.items() if expires_at <= now
155        ]
156        for state in expired:
157            del self._entries[state]

In-memory reference implementation of OidcStateStore (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).

Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement OidcStateStore yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes this class.

Thread-safe: guarded by a single threading.Lock so concurrent sync and async (via asyncio's default single-threaded event loop, or a thread-pool-offloaded call) callers never corrupt the underlying dict.

def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure: 
173def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure:
174    """Map a platform ceremony error to its canonical classification (§24.6b
175    rule 5).
176
177    Accepts anything a caller can get hold of: an exception, an error name
178    relayed from a browser or an Android ``CreateCredentialException``, an
179    ``ASAuthorizationError`` code by name. Everything unrecognized is
180    :attr:`WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN` rather than a raise — a classifier that can
181    fail is one more thing for an error handler to handle.
182    """
183    if isinstance(error, str):
184        name: str | None = error
185    elif isinstance(error, BaseException):
186        name = type(error).__name__
187    else:
188        name = getattr(error, "name", None)
189        if not isinstance(name, str):
190            name = None
191    if name is None:
192        return WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN
193    return _FAILURE_BY_NAME.get(name.strip().lower(), WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN)

203    return _FAILURE_MESSAGES[failure]

def webauthn_request_json( challenge: WebauthnChallenge | dict[str, typing.Any]) -> str: 
206def webauthn_request_json(challenge: WebauthnChallenge | dict[str, Any]) -> str:
207    """The challenge in the JSON form every platform authenticator API takes
208    (§24.6a rule 1).
209
210    This is the string an Android app passes to
211    ``CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest`` or ``GetPublicKeyCredentialOption``,
212    and the value a browser passes to
213    ``PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()``. It is the inner
214    options object: the ``publicKey`` wrapper belongs to the DOM's
215    ``CredentialCreationOptions`` and the platform JSON APIs do not want it.
216
217    Pure local computation, no I/O. Nothing is defaulted, dropped or reordered
218    on the way through (§24.0).
219    """
220    raw = challenge.challenge if isinstance(challenge, WebauthnChallenge) else challenge
221    return json.dumps(raw.get("publicKey", raw), separators=(",", ":"))

The result of oidc_par (CONTRACT.md §26.1).

The server answered 201 — RFC 9126 §2.2 specifies Created, and a success predicate written == 200 would treat every successful push as a failure.

state, nonce and code_verifier are carried straight through from the AuthorizationRequest that was pushed: §26.2 rule 1 forbids a second generator, and rule 6 wants exactly one code_verifier so there is no second place for the two to disagree.
